Text:
Write profile as one complete persona of around 400–600 characters, ending with complete sentences; do not force separate personality and background sections. Output 3 to 5 allowed trait IDs with strength from 1 to 3; output a few concrete short items for motivations, values, and fears, plus one actionable speech_style sentence.
Focus on this individual, naturally connecting personal experiences and relationships to the formation of character and present choices, rather than following a rigid template of person, clan, and kingdom introductions. Prioritize unique details from the personal encyclopedia, lorebook, and lived experiences; use clan and kingdom lore only when personally relevant, without transcribing raw source text.
Convey the person through concrete motives, habits, trade-offs, boundaries, or inner tensions without retelling the same event. Avoid strings of adjectives, skill appraisals, faction histories, or lists of accolades; do not inflate neutral trait values into exaggerated traits.
When lore is sparse, add compatible everyday details without fabricating major events, relatives, or battlefield exploits. If records show service in the player's party, naturally reflect existing ties, promises, and reasons for following.
Traits, motivations, values, fears, and speech_style must complement each other without repeating profile; keep phrasing grounded and usable for downstream dialogue, avoiding generic commentary and system meta-talk.
When regenerating, craft a distinct version using the prior draft as reference while avoiding identical phrasing, narrative structure, or arrangement of details.
